`cppODE()` computes the sensitivities $S = \partial x/\partial\theta$ of
the trajectory by dual numbers, under error control. Symbols are those of
the [notation table](methods-overview.html#notation). R interface:
`deriv` and `derivMode` of
[`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html) and `tangent` and `sensErrCon`
of [`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html).

## Dual-number arithmetic

Sensitivities come from forward-mode automatic differentiation
[@griewank2008evaluating], not finite differences. Arithmetic and
elementary functions are overloaded for the *dual number*
$$
  \tilde x = x + x'\,\varepsilon,
  \qquad \varepsilon^2 = 0,\quad \varepsilon \ne 0,
$$
with primal value $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and directional derivative
$x' \in \mathbb{R}$, so the C++ source of $f$ compiles unchanged for
primal and sensitivities. As a first-order Taylor expansion in
$\varepsilon$, with $\tilde y = y + y'\varepsilon$,
$$
  \tilde x + \tilde y = (x+y) + (x'+y')\varepsilon,
  \qquad
  \tilde x \cdot \tilde y = xy + (xy' + x'y)\varepsilon,
$$
and for any smooth scalar function $g$,
$$
  g(\tilde x) = g(x) + g'(x)\,x'\,\varepsilon.
$$
By composition, $f$ called with dual inputs returns $f$ with the
directional derivative.

## Tangent storage

A dual holds a value and a run-time number of tangent slots. A
second-order dual nests a dual in a dual and propagates only the lower
triangle of the Hessian. The state vectors kept across steps are
allocated once per solve, so memory does not grow with the number of
steps.

## Sensitivity equations by dual evaluation

For a right-hand side depending on parameters
$p \in \mathbb{R}^{n_p}$,
$$
  \dot x = f(x, p, t), \qquad x(t_0) = x_0(p),
$$
the *sensitivity matrix* is
$$
  S_p = \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_x \times n_p},
  \qquad
  (S_p)_{ij} = \frac{\partial x_i}{\partial p_j}.
$$
Seeding state $i$ with row $i$ of $S_p$ gives
$$
  \tilde x_i = x_i + (S_p)_{ij}\,\varepsilon_j,
$$
with dual unit $\varepsilon_j$ for direction $p_j$ and summation over
repeated indices. The $\varepsilon_j$-coefficient of the $i$-th output
of $f$ evaluated over the dual algebra is
$$
  \bigl[f(\tilde x, p, t)\bigr]_{i,\,\varepsilon_j}
  = \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_k}\,(S_p)_{kj}
    + \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial p_j}.
$$
Differentiating the primal part $\dot x_i = f_i(x,p,t)$ in $p_j$
identifies this coefficient with $\dot{(S_p)}_{ij}$:
[]{#eq-sensitivity-p}
$$
  \dot S_p
    = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\,S_p
      + \frac{\partial f}{\partial p},
  \qquad
  S_p(t_0) = \frac{\partial x_0}{\partial p}. \tag{1}
$$
One dual evaluation of $f$ gives [(1)](#eq-sensitivity-p) for all
columns, at a cost proportional to $n_p$, without forming
$\partial f/\partial x$.

## Seeding of the tangent

For a reparametrization $(x_0, p) = \Phi(\theta)$,
$\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M$,
$$
  S_\theta = \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta}
           \in \mathbb{R}^{n_x \times M},
$$
and by the chain rule [(1)](#eq-sensitivity-p) becomes
[]{#eq-sensitivity-theta}
$$
  \dot S_\theta
    = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\,S_\theta
      + \frac{\partial f}{\partial p}
        \,\frac{\partial p}{\partial \theta},
  \qquad
  S_\theta(t_0) = \frac{\partial x_0}{\partial \theta}. \tag{2}
$$
The *tangent* $\partial (x_0, p) / \partial\theta$ is the `tangent`
argument of `solveODE()`, fixed during integration. The identity tangent
gives $\theta = (x_0, p)$. Each direction costs one state vector.

## Error norm with sensitivities

Every step produces $1+M$ error vectors of length $n_x$: $e^{(x)}$ for
the state, with norm [Stepping (8)](methods-stepping.html#eq-wrms), and
$e_S^{(k)}$ for each column $\partial x/\partial \theta_k$, with
$S_\theta$ in place of $x$ in error vector and weight,
[]{#eq-wrms-col}
$$
  \| e_S^{(k)} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}} =
  \sqrt{\frac{1}{n_x} \sum_{i=1}^{n_x} \left(
    \frac{(e_S)_{ik}}{w^{(k)}_{i}}
  \right)^{\!2}},
  \qquad
  w^{(k)}_{i} = \mathtt{abstol} + \mathtt{reltol}\,|(S_\theta)_{ik}^{\mathrm{ref}}|, \tag{3}
$$
with $(S_\theta)_{ik}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ taken like $x^{\mathrm{ref}}$:
the accepted value for multistep methods, the maximum over both step ends
for single-step methods. As in CVODES, the controller uses the largest
norm,
[]{#eq-wrms-sens}
$$
  \| e_{n+1} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}} = \max\left\{
    \| e^{(x)} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}},\;
    \max_{1 \le k \le M} \| e_S^{(k)} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}}
  \right\}. \tag{4}
$$
A flat WRMS over all $n_x(1+M)$ components would let small errors in some
columns mask a large one in another; the maximum holds each direction to the
tolerance. The BDF/NDF corrector uses the same
maximum, so an unconverged sensitivity direction forces further
iterations or a smaller step. With `sensErrCon = FALSE`, error test,
order selection, corrector test and initial-step estimate use the state
only, and steps and iteration counts are those of a value run.

## Corrector iterations {#corrector}

In `bdf` and `adams` the iterations
[Stepping (3)](methods-stepping.html#eq-newton) run on dual numbers: each
tangent takes the iterations of the values, against the same $W$ and
without the derivative of $W$, which like the step size is a solver
decision. With `sensErrCon = FALSE` the sensitivities are the derivative
of the computed solution on the grid of a value run, as the reverse mode
returns
([Reverse mode](methods-reverse.html#discrete-and-continuous-adjoints)).
